Gridded data

Besides being interpolated to the station locations, a model can be loaded as gridded data: its original output, read on the model grid.

Gridded data can be used in the dashboard, report and library modes. It is only drawn on the map: it is not used in any other plot type or in the statistics.

Loading gridded data

Dashboard

In the MODELS menu, each model has an interpolated and a gridded column. A model can be checked in both columns at the same time, to compare its interpolated values at the stations with its grid. Only one gridded model can be loaded at a time: if a second one is checked, it is unchecked again and a warning names the gridded model already checked.

If only gridded data is loaded (no observations or interpolated models), the map statistic menus and the station selection options are disabled, as there are no stations to show. Gridded models are never offered in the map Dataset 1 and Dataset 2 menus, as they have no data at the stations: the lead days drawn on the grid are chosen with Forecast grid lead days in the map settings menu (see Forecast data).

Configuration files (dashboard, report and library)

Add ::gridded at the end of the model name:

model = cams61_emep_ph2-eu-000::gridded

To load the same model both interpolated and gridded, list it twice. Models without a tag are read as interpolated, which can also be set explicitly with ::interpolated:

model = cams61_emep_ph2-eu-000, cams61_emep_ph2-eu-000::gridded

Only one gridded model can be loaded at a time. If more are set, the first one is used.

Where gridded files are read from

Gridded files are searched for in the paths defined in settings/interp_models.yaml, and in mod_to_interp_root, defined in settings/data_paths.yaml.

Gridded data is only read when clicking READ or when loading a configuration file. If some days of the selected period have no valid gridded data (e.g. a forecast run or a file is missing), a warning is shown, as they are not drawn on the grid.

Forecast data

Gridded data is read for the same forecast days selected for its interpolated version (e.g. days 2 and 4 for day2, day4, or the selected days for daily and combined), never for the ones of other models. If no forecast option is set, only the first forecast day is read, as for interpolated data.

When forecast options are set in the model name, a gridded model loaded with its interpolated version must have the same one as it (e.g. a59g-regional-000-day3, a59g-regional-000-day3::gridded).

The forecast option and lead days used are shown next to the gridded model in the terminal when reading, e.g. a59g-regional-000::gridded (day option with data from lead days 2 and 4), or a59g-regional-000::gridded (with data from lead day 1) when no forecast option is applied to it.

Lead day N of a forecast run covers the 24 hours that start N-1 days after the run starts, e.g. lead day 1 of the run of 2023010100 covers 2023-01-01 00:00 to 2023-01-01 23:00. Forecast runs are expected to be 24 hours apart: a missing run leaves days without data for its lead days (see above).

Gridded models that are not forecast models (their files are not forecast runs, e.g. cams61_emep_ph2-eu-000) have no lead days, so what follows about lead days does not apply to them:

  • nothing is shown next to them in the terminal (e.g. cams61_emep_ph2-eu-000::gridded),

  • their map title has no lead day (e.g. cams61_emep_ph2-eu-000 (gridded)),

  • map_grid_forecast_lead_days is not used (with a warning),

  • in the dashboard, the Forecast grid lead days drop-down is empty and disabled, while their grid is still drawn.

See Forecast for the forecast options.

The table describes report and library modes, where the data selected for the map (z1 in reports, labela in library) chooses the lead day drawn. In the dashboard, the grid shows the lead days checked in Forecast grid lead days instead, whatever is selected for the map (see “Dashboard: forecast grid lead days” below).

X is any number from 1 to N. In the legend, a filled dot marks the interpolated data and an empty square the gridded data.

Gridded models are only shown in the legend next to a map drawn over their grid: in the dashboard, and in library mode on maps with the domain option (the only maps with a legend). In other library plots, in the library legend plot, and in reports, where the legend is only shown on plots of station data, gridded models are left out of the legend.

Each map also describes its grid in its title (see Map title).

With day, each lead day is a separate entry, so in report and library modes the grid always shows a single lead day: the one of the selected entry. With daily and combined, all lead days are merged into one entry, so the grid shows the average of the loaded lead days, which is that same day when only one is loaded.

In report and library modes, when the observations or another model are selected for the map, they have no lead day of their own, so the grid shows the average of the loaded lead days (lead day 1 if no forecast option is set). For example, with day2, day4, the grid under the fc-day2 map shows lead day 2, while the grid under the observations map shows the average of lead days 2 and 4.

daily and combined only differ in the timeseries plot: on the map, both the stations and the grid show the mean over all loaded lead days.

If a model is loaded gridded only, it has its own forecast options, and its grid uses their lead days:

  • With day, it gets one label per lead day, e.g. fc-day2 (gridded) and fc-day4 (gridded) for day2, day4, and each lead day gets its own map in reports, showing the observations over the grid of that lead day, as the gridded model has no data at the stations.

  • With daily and combined, it keeps its label (e.g. fc (gridded)) and the grid shows the average of the selected lead days.

As it has no data at the stations, it does not switch the plots of station data to the forecast layout (e.g. the daily timeseries per forecast day): only models with forecast data at the stations do. Where gridded models are shown in the legend, its entry is shown with a square only. In day mode, only the lead days drawn on the grid are shown.

Choosing the grid lead days

In report and library modes, map_grid_forecast_lead_days chooses which of the loaded lead days are averaged on the grid, given as numbers or forecast days (e.g. 2, 4 or day2, day4).

It is set per section and replaces the average of all loaded lead days on maps that have no lead day of their own: maps of the observations, of other models, and of daily or combined entries. Maps of a single forecast day in day mode (e.g. fc-day2) keep their own lead day, and a warning says so.

For example, with day1, day2, day4 and map_grid_forecast_lead_days = 2, 4, the grid under the observations map shows the average of lead days 2 and 4, while the grid under the fc-day1 map still shows lead day 1.

Lead days that were not loaded are left out with a warning, and if none of them was loaded, the grid uses all loaded lead days. If no gridded data is loaded, or the gridded model is not a forecast model, the field is not used and a warning is shown.

In the dashboard, the field sets the lead days checked in Forecast grid lead days when the configuration file is loaded (at launch or from the toolbar), following the same rules. Afterwards, the lead days checked follow the drop-down (see below): reading again does not apply the field, and it is not written when saving a configuration file.

Dashboard: forecast grid lead days

In the dashboard, the Forecast grid lead days drop-down in the map settings menu lists the lead days read for the gridded model (1 if it is not read with a forecast option), and the grid shows the average of the checked ones. If the gridded model is not a forecast model, the drop-down is empty and disabled, and the grid is always drawn.

It does not depend on the data selected in Dataset 1: for example, with day2, day4, the grid shows the average of lead days 2 and 4 under every map until one of them is unchecked.

The map title and the legend follow the checked lead days. If none is checked, no grid is drawn.

After reading, all lead days are checked if the models have changed (e.g. a model added or its forecast days changed in the MODELS menu), otherwise the previous selection is kept. When a configuration file with map_grid_forecast_lead_days is loaded, its lead days are checked instead (see Choosing the grid lead days).

Period

In the dashboard, the grid shows the period selected for the map. In report and library modes, it shows all the loaded period.

Map title

When a grid is drawn under a map, the map title names the gridded model and the lead days drawn (no lead days if the gridded model is not a forecast model, e.g. cams61_emep_ph2-eu-000 (gridded)), so it is clear what the grid shows even when it belongs to another model.

The gridded model is shown by its alias if one is set in the configuration file. Maps without a grid (e.g. bias maps) keep their usual title.

  • Report: on its own line, under the data label:

    fc-day2
fc (gridded, lead day 2)
SECTION (1751 stations)

  • Library: at the end of the title, after a +, e.g. observations Mean at 1751 stations + fc (gridded, mean of lead days 2 and 4). It is not added when a title is passed with title.

  • Dashboard: on its own line, under the number of selected stations, e.g. fc (gridded, mean of lead days 2 and 4).

Stations over the grid

When a grid is drawn under the stations, the station markers get an edge to tell them apart from the grid. On maps without a grid, the stations are drawn without it. The edge is set with the stations_over_grid variable, under plot in the map section of the plot characteristics file, for each mode:

"plot":
  {
    "stations": { "s": 20, "picker": 1, "zorder": 5, "linewidth": 0 },
    "stations_over_grid": { "edgecolor": "black", "linewidth": 0.4 },
    "grid": { "zorder": 2, "alpha": null },
  }

stations_over_grid is applied on top of stations when a grid is drawn, so any marker property can be changed over the grid. If it is not set (e.g. in a custom plot characteristics file made before it was added), the stations look the same with and without a grid.

Limitations

  • Only the Mean statistic can be drawn on the grid. Other statistics show a message and no grid is drawn.

  • The grid is not drawn on bias maps (when two datasets are selected for the map), as it is an absolute field.

  • Resampling and temporal colocation are not applied to gridded data. A warning is shown in the dashboard if they are active.

  • Filters only apply to stations, so they do not change the grid.
